BASE.name: ATTACK_VECTOR
BASE.justification: Exploited via Salesforce REST/SOAP APIs over the internet using a misconfigured Connected App OAuth scope.

BASE.name: ATTACK_COMPLEXITY
BASE.justification: No special conditions are required; exploitation is straightforward once a valid OAuth token is obtained.

BASE.name: PRIVILEGES_REQUIRED
BASE.justification: Attacker must obtain a valid OAuth access token for the Connected App, requiring minimal privilege.

BASE.name: USER_INTERACTION
BASE.justification: Once an OAuth token is issued, no further user action is needed for exploitation.

BASE.name: SCOPE
BASE.justification: The Full OAuth scope extends access beyond the Connected App boundary to the entire Salesforce organization.

BASE.name: CONFIDENTIALITY
BASE.justification: The Full scope exposes all organizational data including records, files, and metadata to unauthorized access.

BASE.name: INTEGRITY
BASE.justification: The Full scope permits unrestricted data creation, modification, and deletion across the entire Salesforce org.

BASE.name: AVAILABILITY
BASE.justification: Bulk API calls are possible via the Full scope, but the primary threat is data access and manipulation rather than service outage.

TEMPORAL.name: EXPLOIT_CODE_MATURITY
TEMPORAL.justification: OAuth token abuse techniques are publicly documented and demonstrable; no specialized weaponized tooling is required.

TEMPORAL.name: REMEDIATION_LEVEL
TEMPORAL.justification: Salesforce officially supports granular OAuth scope restriction; remediation is well-documented and straightforward.

TEMPORAL.name: REPORT_CONFIDENCE
TEMPORAL.justification: Statically confirmed by CodeScan parser; the presence of <scopes>Full</scopes> is deterministic and unambiguous.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_ATTACK_VECTOR
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Exploitation occurs over the internet via Salesforce OAuth APIs — mirrors base AV.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_ATTACK_COMPLEXITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: No additional complexity in the deployed environment — mirrors base AC.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_PRIVILEGES_REQUIRED
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: A valid OAuth token is still required in any environment — mirrors base PR.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_USER_INTERACTION
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: No user interaction required in any deployment context — mirrors base UI.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_SCOPE
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Full scope still crosses the Connected App boundary into the entire org — mirrors base S.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_CONFIDENTIALITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: All org data remains exposed regardless of environment — mirrors base C.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_INTEGRITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Unrestricted data modification capability persists in all environments — mirrors base I.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_AVAILABILITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Bulk API abuse potential remains low impact in deployment — mirrors base A.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: CONFIDENTIALITY_REQUIREMENT
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Connected Apps with Full OAuth scope expose organizational records and API data; while sensitive, the data is business-operational rather than classified or life-critical, warranting a medium confidentiality requirement.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: INTEGRITY_REQUIREMENT
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: The Full scope allows data modification across the org, but the Connected App operates within standard Salesforce business workflows rather than safety-critical or regulated systems, making integrity important but not at the highest requirement level.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: AVAILABILITY_REQUIREMENT
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Availability is not the primary threat vector for this rule; data exposure and manipulation are the core concerns.
